heard: 21 Sikh soldiers stood against 10,000. In September of 1897, the isolated Saragari outposts faced overwhelming danger on the frontier. Havil dar Asharsim commanded the small garrison holding the communication lines. Enemies created a thick smoke screen by burning bushes near the outer walls. Gurmukh Singh signaled live updates across the valley as the fortress walls fell. Every brave man perished in history's greatest stand protecting the frontier. 10,000 tribesmen surrounded 21 Sikh soldiers who stood against them.
